body: The device key goes into the local cache *before* `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, and it stays cached even when that call returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. So the first request from a device over the limit gets rejected, but every request from that device for the next ~29 minutes hits the cache, `tagDeviceUI` returns nil, and `Authenticate` lets it through. That defeats the limit. Only cache the key after the DB write succeeds, or cache the limit-reached result too so later requests are rejected the same way.

The count check and the insert below aren't atomic. Concurrent first requests from several new devices can all see `count < limit` and all get inserted, so the limit goes over by as many requests as are in flight. That matters now that this is enforced in the auth path. If a hard limit is intended, do the check and insert in one transaction or conditional insert; otherwise document that the limit is approximate.

When a limit is set, every uncached device tag now runs a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` before the upsert. Tagging also moved from a background goroutine into the synchronous request path (see client.go), so this count plus the write now add latency to anonymous requests. The count also runs for devices that already exist, where a plain update would do. Consider trying the update first and only counting or inserting when no row was updated.

Tagging used to run asynchronously with its own timeout and panic recovery. Now it runs inline on the request context, so every uncached anonymous request waits on DB writes (and the extra count query), and a panic in tagging is no longer recovered here. Also, the limit only applies when the client sends the device-id header: `TagDevice` returns nil when the header is missing, so a client can skip the limit by leaving the header out. If the limit is meant to be enforced, it can't depend on a client-supplied header being present.

This returns the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which isn't an `errutil`/authn error. So the user probably gets a generic 500 or 401 with no useful message instead of a clear 'anonymous device limit reached' response. Wrap it in a proper errutil error (for example Unauthorized or Forbidden with a public message) so the frontend can tell this case apart.

The store is now built inside the service instead of injected, but `pkg/server/wire.go` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), ...)`. `ProvideAnonDBStore` now needs an `int64` that no provider supplies, so wire generation or the build will fail, and the bind is now unused. Remove those wire entries, or better, keep injecting the store and have `ProvideAnonDBStore` take `*setting.Cfg`.

`rowsAffected == 0` isn't a reliable signal that the limit was reached. On MySQL, `RowsAffected` counts only rows that actually changed by default, not rows matched. If an existing device sends a request with the same IP and user agent within the same second (MySQL `DATETIME` has second precision), the UPDATE changes nothing, returns 0, and a legitimate, already-registered device gets rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

`anonymousDeviceExpiration` is now defined in both `api.go` and `anonstore/database.go`, and `impl.go` still uses its own `thirtyDays`. Export a single constant from `anonstore` so the expiry window used for counting, listing and enforcing the limit can't drift apart.
